newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast cracks down on cotton textile fraud.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast cracks down on cotton textile fraud.

text.p: Ivory Coast has seized illegal cotton textiles and will fine traders after local industry complaints about false customs declarations and fakes.
"Sanctions for fraud in this sector could mean not only imprisonment but expulsion of non-Ivorians who continue to carry on activities," a cabinet statement said on Wednesday.
A total of 3,836 rolls of textile worth 26 million CFA ($46,000) had been seized from eight traders, mostly Lebanese and Malians, it said.

Ivory Coast is grooming its cotton manufacturing industry for privatisation but it says the cotton sector had faced "certain difficulties despite competitive gains after devaluation of the CFA franc in 1994."
The sale of textiles without correct origin denomination is illegal in Ivory Coast under 1992 laws.
Traders face fines of up to half the value of seized goods.
Laws dating back to 1992 would be reviewed to deal with "fraud, unfair competition, distribution network rules and protection of industrial and intellectual property," the statement said.
